name: Richard II
description: Born January 1367 at Bordeaux; crowned King of England 16 July 1377 at age ten, on the death of his grandfather Edward III (his father, Edward the Black Prince, had died in 1376). Governed in his minority by a series of continual councils dominated by his uncles, chiefly John of Gaunt. Fourteen years old during the 1381 revolt. Personally rode out to meet the rebels twice -- at Mile End on 14 June and at Smithfield on 15 June -- and issued charters at Mile End promising the abolition of serfdom, which the royal council revoked within weeks (writs of revocation issued by 2 July 1381). Later reign (he is deposed and dies in 1400) is outside this book's scope; contemporaries and later historians alike read his conduct during the revolt -- both the personal courage at Smithfield and the bad faith of the revocation -- as an early sign of the autocratic style that eventually cost him his throne.
narrative_function: The Crown; the figure the rebels appeal to directly, over the heads of his ministers, at Mile End and Smithfield.
